data.description:
## Symptom

When a collapse replays any commit above the boundary, the ledger-anchor commit is not an ancestor of the rewritten tip. The rewritten branch runs checkpoint → first replayed commit. The ledger anchor is a side child of the checkpoint that nothing references, and the collapse deletes its scratch ref, so the anchor ends up unreachable.

`CollapseResult.enforce_since` is that anchor. `verify_authorship._is_enforced` (`src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:258`) enforces an event only when `git merge-base --is-ancestor <since_ref> <event commit>` succeeds. That never happens for an unreachable anchor, so every event in the rewritten history is grandfathered. `verify-identity` then passes without checking any signature.

## Evidence

- **Synthetic probe, 2026-11-17.** Built from `tests/unit/test_reclaim_collapse.py::_build_collapsible_store`, with 1 replayed commit. The result was `anchor_is_ancestor_of_tip False` and `enforce_since == ledger_anchor_sha True`. The same result came from the current engine (origin/main 57d45053272) and from the original S1 engine (a758402f065, ticket `filmable-crushing-nighthawk`). The defect predates the streamed rewrite (`silk-unpleasant-jackal`), which reproduced the original behaviour exactly.
- **Real-scale dry run, 2026-11-16.** On a TMPDIR copy of `origin/tickets` at e7a0476397f, the rewritten root 9ecfe8768a5 has exactly one child, b04372602ca. That child is a replayed `reconciler: persist binding-store snapshot` commit. `git log --grep "reconcile authorship ledger" tickets` finds nothing.
- **Why the existing test passes.** `test_enforce_since_reanchor_makes_verify_authorship_clean` collapses with the tip equal to the boundary. No commit is replayed, so the anchor is the tip and the defect is hidden.

## Cause

In `_StreamedRewrite._replay`, and in the original `_rewritten_parents`, the boundary maps to the checkpoint (`old_to_new[boundary] = checkpoint_sha`). A replayed commit whose original parent is the boundary is therefore parented on the checkpoint, not on the ledger anchor (`current_tip` at that point).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After a collapse that replays at least one commit, `ledger_anchor_sha` is an ancestor of `rewritten_tip`, and `enforce_since` names a commit on the rewritten branch. A new test in `tests/unit/test_reclaim_collapse.py` with replayed commits shows this.
- [ ] With replayed commits and `REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE=<enforce_since>`, `verify-identity --all` enforces the replayed events. A test shows an unsigned replayed event failing the gate under `REBAR_IDENTITY_REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATED=1`.
data.title: Reclaim collapse leaves the ledger-anchor commit off the rewritten branch, so enforce_since grandfathers every event
